statement:
The function
$$f(x)=\frac23 x^3+2mx^2+n, \qquad m>0$$
has three distinct real roots.

What is the complete range of possible values of $n$, in terms of $m$?
solution:
A cubic has three distinct real roots exactly when it has two stationary points, one above and one below the $x$-axis.

Differentiate:
$$f'(x)=2x^2+4mx=2x(x+2m),$$
so the stationary points are at $x=0$ and $x=-2m$.

Evaluate $f$ at these points:
$$f(0)=n, \qquad f(-2m)=\frac23(-8m^3)+2m(4m^2)+n=-\frac{16}{3}m^3+8m^3+n=\frac83 m^3+n.$$

For three distinct real roots, the two values $n$ and $\frac83m^3+n$ must have opposite signs. Since $m>0$, we have $\frac83m^3+n>n$, so we need $n<0$ and $\frac83m^3+n>0$. The second inequality gives $n>-\frac83m^3$. Hence
$$-\frac83m^3<n<0,$$
which is **option A**.

hints: A cubic has three real roots iff its two stationary points straddle the x-axis.
Find f'(x)=0 to locate the stationary points.
Require f(0) and f(-2m) to have opposite signs.
